resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives a 100-foot steel tower; the 1959 Coast and Geodetic Survey description gives an overall height of 110 feet. The record keeps the Register's 100 feet (30.5 m) and the story says the sources disagree.

The Register says open seven days a week from Memorial Day through October 15; the Minnesota Historical Society says closed November through May. Both are reported and visitors should check the center's hours.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record was right on county (Cass) and on relocated status. The original Bena site has only the 1959 survey as a locator; no source we read describes what is there now. Forest Lookouts gives no build year, so 1934 rests on the Register and the Minnesota Historical Society. The 110-foot figure is an overall height from a 1959 survey, not a later measurement. The current tower and its climbing rules are covered in us-mn-boulder-hill-at-forest-history-center; facts.staffing and facts.access here describe that current tower. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story no longer says the MNHS ties towers like this one to the state's response, and the 1959 survey location is about half a mile south of U.S. Highway 2, not 'just south'.
